title: [Feature Request] Process isolation and better crash attribution for third-party plasma widgets
line: When a widget you installed yourself crashes Plasma, Plasma now names it in the log and keeps it disabled until the next start, instead of crashing over and over.
explanation: Third-party widgets run inside plasmashell, so a widget that crashes it usually crashes it again on every restart until systemd gives up and the desktop and panels are gone, and nothing in the log says which widget did it. Also, an applet marked as failed before its item was created still had its QML created and run behind the error message. plasmashell now installs a KCrash emergency function: if the crash happens on the main thread while QML code from a widget installed in the user's own plasma/plasmoids folder is on the JavaScript stack, it prints "crashed while running code of the widget <id>" and records the id; on the next start that widget shows the usual error placeholder ("... was disabled because it caused Plasma to crash. It will be loaded again the next time Plasma starts."), and libplasma no longer runs the QML of an applet that is already marked as failed.

commits.message:
shell: disable a widget for one session after it crashes Plasma

A user-installed widget that crashed Plasma usually crashed it again on
every restart, and nothing said which widget it was. The crash handler
now logs it, and the next start shows it as disabled instead of loading.

BUG: 528864

plasmaquick: don't create the QML of an applet that failed to launch

When an applet was already marked as failed, its QML still got created
and completed behind the error message, and an empty list of QML errors
replaced the reason in the details. Skip its QML and keep the reason.

BUG: 528864

media.caption: Master: a user-installed widget whose native code crashes; plasmashell crashes, restarts, crashes again three times and then stays down
With the fix: it crashes once, and the restarted Plasma shows the widget as disabled and stays up
Master after the crash loop: no desktop and no panel
With the fix: the widget's place shows why it was disabled; the rest of Plasma works
